<sso>Cloudron SSO can be added as an external identity provider via Settings > Identity Providers in the NetBird dashboard after initial setup.</sso>

STUN_PORT.title: STUN (NAT traversal)

manifest.postInstallMessage:
NetBird is running. Visit the app URL to access the dashboard.

On first run, you will see the setup page where you can create your admin account.

Connect clients with `netbird up --management-url https://${CLOUDRON_APP_DOMAIN}:${NETBIRD_PORT} --setup-key YOUR_SETUP_KEY`. Keep TCP port ${NETBIRD_PORT} enabled and accessible for native client traffic.

UDP port ${STUN_PORT} must be accessible from your NetBird clients for NAT traversal.

<sso>Cloudron SSO can be added as an external identity provider via Settings > Identity Providers in the NetBird dashboard after initial setup.</sso>
manifest.changelog:
* Add a dedicated TLS-enabled TCP port for native NetBird management, signal, and relay traffic.
* Keep the dashboard and REST API on Cloudron HTTPS while advertising the selected native client port.
* Document that Cloudron TURN cannot replace NetBird relay authentication and that Reverse Proxy clusters still require public TLS passthrough.

NETBIRD_PORT.description: TLS port for native NetBird management, signal, and relay traffic.

PROXY_PORT.description: Raw TLS backend for the documented second-IP host bridge. Keep disabled until host firewall protection is installed.

STUN_PORT.title: Optional dedicated STUN
STUN_PORT.description: Leave disabled to use Cloudron's platform STUN service. Enable only to run NetBird's own STUN server on this UDP port; it must not be 3478 when Cloudron TURN uses that port.

manifest.postInstallMessage:
NetBird is running. Visit the app URL to access the dashboard.

On first run, create and test the embedded owner account before adding another login method.

Connect clients with `netbird up --management-url https://${CLOUDRON_APP_DOMAIN}:${NETBIRD_PORT} --setup-key YOUR_SETUP_KEY`. Keep TCP port ${NETBIRD_PORT} enabled and accessible for native client traffic.

NAT traversal uses Cloudron's platform STUN service unless you enabled the optional dedicated STUN port.

<sso>Cloudron SSO credentials are available to configure manually in NetBird under Settings > Identity Providers. Keep embedded owner access as the recovery login.</sso>
manifest.changelog:
* Use Cloudron's platform STUN service by default; new installs no longer need a dedicated STUN UDP port.
* Make the dedicated STUN port optional; existing installs keep their binding and NetBird's own STUN server.
* Keep NetBird's built-in relay for peers that cannot connect directly; Cloudron's TURN relay and secret are not used.
* Trust forwarded client addresses only from the in-container proxies.
* Update to Cloudron base 6.0.0 and dashboard v2.94.0.

NETBIRD_PORT.description: TLS port for native NetBird management, signal, and relay traffic.

PROXY_PORT.title: Optional reverse-proxy ingress
PROXY_PORT.description: Raw TLS backend for the documented second-IP host bridge. Keep disabled until host firewall protection is installed.

STUN_PORT.title: Optional dedicated STUN
STUN_PORT.description: Leave disabled to use Cloudron's platform STUN service. Enable only to run NetBird's own STUN server on this UDP port; it must not be 3478 when Cloudron TURN uses that port.

manifest.postInstallMessage:
NetBird is running. Visit the app URL to access the dashboard.

On first run, create and test the embedded owner account before adding another login method.

Connect clients with `netbird up --management-url https://${CLOUDRON_APP_DOMAIN}:${NETBIRD_PORT} --setup-key YOUR_SETUP_KEY`. Keep TCP port ${NETBIRD_PORT} enabled and accessible for native client traffic.

NAT traversal uses Cloudron's platform STUN service unless you enabled the optional dedicated STUN port.

<sso>Cloudron SSO credentials are available to configure manually in NetBird under Settings > Identity Providers. Keep embedded owner access as the recovery login.</sso>
manifest.changelog:
* Native NetBird clients can now connect over IPv6 on IPv6-enabled servers; previously only IPv4 worked.
* Add an external monitoring guide with a recommended updown.io check plan for the app, native port and optional proxy.

PROXY_PORT.title: Optional reverse-proxy ingress
PROXY_PORT.description: Raw TLS backend for the documented second-IP host bridge. Keep disabled until host firewall protection is installed.

manifest.postInstallMessage:
NetBird is running. Visit the app URL to access the dashboard.

On first run, create and test the embedded owner account before adding another login method.

Connect clients with `netbird up --management-url https://${CLOUDRON_APP_DOMAIN}:${NETBIRD_PORT} --setup-key YOUR_SETUP_KEY --enable-rosenpass`. Keep TCP port ${NETBIRD_PORT} enabled and accessible for native client traffic.

The client port accepts only post-quantum TLS, so use NetBird clients 0.61.0 or later. `--enable-rosenpass` adds post-quantum keys to device tunnels and only connects to other Rosenpass devices, so use it on every device.

NAT traversal uses Cloudron's platform STUN service unless you enabled the optional dedicated STUN port.

<sso>Cloudron SSO credentials are available to configure manually in NetBird under Settings > Identity Providers. Keep embedded owner access as the recovery login.</sso>
manifest.changelog:
* The native client port now accepts only post-quantum TLS 1.3 (X25519MLKEM768), so recorded client traffic can't be decrypted later by a quantum computer. NetBird clients older than 0.61.0 can no longer connect unless you set the NETBIRD_TLS_ALLOW_CLASSIC=true app environment variable.
* Setup instructions now include --enable-rosenpass for post-quantum device tunnels. See docs/POST-QUANTUM.md for migrating existing devices and auditing them.

manifest.postInstallMessage:
NetBird is running. Visit the app URL to access the dashboard.

On first run, create and test the embedded owner account before adding another login method.

Connect clients with `netbird up --management-url https://${CLOUDRON_APP_DOMAIN}:${NETBIRD_PORT} --setup-key YOUR_SETUP_KEY --enable-rosenpass --rosenpass-permissive`, or copy the command from the dashboard's Add Peer dialog, which includes the same flags. Keep TCP port ${NETBIRD_PORT} enabled and accessible for native client traffic.

The client port accepts only post-quantum TLS, so use NetBird clients 0.61.0 or later. The Rosenpass flags add post-quantum keys to tunnels between devices that have it, and still connect to devices that don't. In the desktop app, turn on Enable Quantum-Resistance and Enable Permissive Mode under Settings > Security > Encryption.

NAT traversal uses Cloudron's platform STUN service unless you enabled the optional dedicated STUN port.

<sso>Creating the owner account at /setup also adds Cloudron as a login option. New Cloudron users wait for your approval under Team > Users. Keep the owner account as the recovery login.</sso>
manifest.changelog:
* New installs with Cloudron SSO: creating the owner account at /setup also adds Cloudron as a login option. New Cloudron users need owner approval, and the owner login stays as the recovery login. If adding it fails, setup still works and the log explains the manual steps. Existing installs are unaffected.
* The dashboard's Add Peer command now includes --enable-rosenpass --rosenpass-permissive, so new devices get post-quantum tunnels without losing connections to devices that don't have Rosenpass. Set NETBIRD_CLIENT_ROSENPASS to strict or off to change it.

manifest.changelog:
* Update NetBird server and the optional reverse proxy from 0.81.2 to 0.81.3, including the upstream relay QUIC dependency update.
* Update the dashboard from v2.94.0 to v2.95.0. It adds the certificate posture check editor for NetBird 0.81, per-target HTTP access controls for reverse-proxy services, duplicating policies, and peer search by MAC address. Search engines are now blocked by default via robots.txt.
* Optional second-IP reverse-proxy ingress: the host helper now restores its firewall guard before readiness checks, so a failed check after a reboot keeps the backend port blocked instead of reachable. Copy the released scripts/netbird-ingress.py to /etc/netbird-ingress/ on hosts that use it; an app update alone does not change it.
* Update the Cloudron base image from 6.0.0 to 6.0.1. No configuration changes.
